subject: Request: Vulnerability management evidence & CVE routing (FinTrust)
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@fintrust.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 07 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Vulnerability management evidence & CVE routing (FinTrust)

Hi Lukas,

Hope you’re well — FinTrust is running our quarterly SIG/SOC2 evidence intake this week. We need a short packet that shows Redwood’s vulnerability management posture for our vendor review. Specifically we’re asking for: 

- Scan cadence and types (SCA/static, authenticated network, external perimeter) for the last 6 months;
- CVE remediation SLAs by severity and how exceptions are handled;
- Playbook or routing for newly discovered critical/high CVEs (who is notified, average remediation time, fallback model/policy);
- A short attestation we can include in our SOC2 workpapers that confirms you’ll meet FinTrust’s requirement for high severity fixes within 30 days unless mitigated by compensating controls.

Can you send a single packet (PDF or ZIP) and any supporting spreadsheets by EOD Tuesday (2025-09-09)? If you need to route to a different team, please let me know the owner and expected delivery.

Thanks,
Olivia Grant
Security Operations Manager
FinTrust Financial
security@fintrust.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachment: none

Plan:

- Delivery: target EOD Tuesday (2025-09-09) as requested.

Kimberly — can you confirm the cadence details and attach the latest scan matrix and routing playbook? If we need an expedited SLA commitment for FinTrust beyond standard terms, call it out in your note.

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer

Hi Lukas / Olivia — attaching the packet below. Notes and TL;DR first:

TL;DR
- Scan cadence: external perimeter weekly, authenticated network monthly, SCA (dependency scanning) daily on CI.
- SLAs (standard Redwood policy): Critical: 7 days; High: 30 days; Medium: 90 days; Low: best-effort / next scheduled release. Exceptions are tracked in our ticketing system and require compensating control documentation and SLA exception approval by Security Ops.
- Routing: Critical alerts route to on-call SRE + Security Ops and also trigger an immediate customer notification channel for enterprise customers. High severity routes to vuln-ops queue and product engineering with a 30-day remediation target.

What I’ve attached:
- vm-scan-matrix-2025Q3.csv (spreadsheet showing last six months of scan runs, tool outputs, and sweep coverage)
- cve-routing-playbook.pdf (playbook that describes notification chains, escalation timelines, and exception process)

Attestation (draft):
"Redwood Inference attests that for FinTrust, vulnerabilities classified as High severity will be remediated within 30 calendar days of triage, unless an approved compensating control is documented. Critical vulnerabilities will be remediated within seven calendar days. Exceptions are escalated to Security Ops and recorded in the vulnerability exception registry."

A few clarifying points:
- The 7/30/90 SLA applies to confirmed vulnerabilities in Redwood-managed production components. Third-party vendor dependencies are remediated according to the dependency owner’s cadence; when a dependency fix is required we provide mitigations and a mitigation timeline.
- For enterprise customers who require a shorter SLA for High severity (e.g., 15 days), we can include a contractual exception.
- Evidence: the scan matrix includes sample scan IDs, timestamps, and remediation ticket links (redwood.atlassian.net/TICKET-xxx) — we’ve redacted internal IPs for vendor distribution.

Next steps:
- Lukas: confirm you want the attestation signed and returned as a PDF; we can include Ben on the signature flow.
- Olivia: let us know if you require any additional artifacts (raw scan logs, ticket exports, SOC2 control references).

Attachments: vm-scan-matrix-2025Q3.csv; cve-routing-playbook.pdf

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Lukas / Kimberly — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear packet. The TL;DR and attestation draft look fine to FinTrust’s audit team. A couple quick asks before we close the loop: 

1) Please produce the attestation as a signed PDF we can drop into our control evidence (we’ll accept a signed PDF from an authorized Redwood signatory).
2) Can you confirm whether the 7/30/90 SLAs above are included verbatim in any customer-facing SLA or if they are operational policy only? (We prefer them in a signed addendum or appendix where possible.)

If you can get the signed attestation to me by EOD Wednesday (2025-09-10) we’ll mark this item closed on our intake. I’ve attached a one-page acceptance form — we’ll sign and return once we receive the signed attestation.
